name: Morgan Freeman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Freeman was taking acting classes and working odd jobs in Los Angeles and San Francisco. His Off-Broadway debut came in 1967 at age 30, and his Broadway debut in 1968 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Freeman began acting in school plays as a child in Mississippi and won a statewide drama competition at age 12. He turned down a partial drama scholarship to Jackson State University to enlist in the Air Force in 1955. After leaving the service in 1959, he studied acting at Los Angeles City College and worked as a dancer at the 1964 World's Fair, but did not land a significant professional acting role until his late twenties.
family_context_summary: Born in Memphis, Tennessee to a barber father and mother; raised partly by his grandmother in Mississippi. Working-class family with frequent moves during childhood.
evidence_summary: Freeman showed early acting talent as a child but spent his twenties in the Air Force and then struggling as an acting student and dancer. No significant professional acting milestone occurred before age 26. His career breakthrough came much later with The Electric Company in the 1970s and film roles in the 1980s.

name: Brian Eno
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Roxy Music in 1971 at age 23 and played synthesizer on their debut album (1972) which reached #10 in the UK; launched solo career with two albums by age 25.
early_history_summary: Eno studied at Ipswich School of Art and Winchester School of Art in the 1960s, where he experimented with tape recorders and avant-garde music. He joined Roxy Music in 1971 after being invited to record the band by Andy Mackay, and became their keyboardist and synthesizer player. The band's debut album was released in 1972 to critical acclaim. Eno left Roxy Music in 1973 and immediately released solo albums 'No Pussyfooting' (with Robert Fripp) and 'Here Come the Warm Jets'.
family_context_summary: Born in Woodbridge, Suffolk to a postal worker father (who also repaired clocks) and a Belgian immigrant mother. Working-class family; Eno worked as a postman during school holidays.
parent_family_domain_summary: His grandfather was a multi-instrumentalist who played saxophone and bassoon and repaired pianos and church organs, but Eno's father was a postal worker. No direct parental domain transfer in music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: art school network, Roxy Music collaboration, glam rock wave, tape recorder experimentation
evidence_summary: Eno grew up in a working-class family in Suffolk but gained access to avant-garde music and experimental art through art school education at Ipswich and Winchester. He experimented with tape recorders from the mid-1960s and connected with avant-garde composers like Cornelius Cardew. His invitation to join Roxy Music in 1971 by Andy Mackay, and the complementary partnership with Bryan Ferry, catalyzed his early success. The glam rock wave of the early 1970s provided structural momentum for the band's rapid rise.
starting_point: Born to a postal worker father and Belgian immigrant mother in Woodbridge, Suffolk; raised Catholic in a working-class family with a grandfather who was a multi-instrumentalist.
current_position: Renowned musician, producer, and visual artist credited with creating ambient music; has produced albums for U2, David Bowie, and Talking Heads; estimated net worth ~$60M; lives in London.

trajectory.event: Joined Roxy Music as keyboardist and synthesizer player after being invited by Andy Mackay to record the band.
Roxy Music's self-titled debut album released, reaching #10 in the UK and establishing the band as leaders of the glam rock movement.
Left Roxy Music and launched solo career with 'No Pussyfooting' (with Robert Fripp) and 'Here Come the Warm Jets'.
Released 'Discreet Music', beginning his development of ambient music theory.
Collaborated with David Bowie on the Berlin Trilogy albums (Low, Heroes, Lodger).
Produced U2's 'The Joshua Tree', one of the best-selling albums of all time.
Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Roxy Music.

name: Shinya Yamanaka
milestone_by_age_26: No material research milestone by age 26; Yamanaka received his MD in 1987 and was completing his residency as an orthopedic surgeon. His PhD research began in 1989 and his first significant publication came in 1992.
early_history_summary: Yamanaka studied medicine at Kobe University, graduating with an MD in 1987. He began his career as an orthopedic surgery resident at National Osaka Hospital but found he was not talented in surgery. He did not begin his PhD research in pharmacology until 1989, and his first notable publication in Circulation Research came in 1992 at age 30.
family_context_summary: Born in Osaka, Japan to a father who ran a small factory manufacturing components for sawing machines and a mother who raised the children. Father encouraged him to pursue medicine rather than taking over the family business.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an engineer who designed and manufactured components; no direct medical or research domain transfer.
evidence_summary: Yamanaka was a medical student and surgical resident in his twenties with no significant research milestone by age 26. His Nobel Prize-winning iPS cell research came decades later, starting around 2006. His early career was characterized by a transition from surgery to basic research that only began at age 27.

name: Jan Fabre
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved international breakthrough in 1982 with the performance 'This is theatre as it was to be expected and foreseen', which placed him at the forefront of the European avant-garde theatre scene.
early_history_summary: Fabre studied at the Municipal Institute of Decorative Arts and the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Antwerp. He began creating performance art and solo performances in the late 1970s while still a student, including window performances (1977) and blood drawings (1978). His 'Money Performances' in 1980 involved burning money and writing with ashes. By 1980 he had also begun directing theatre, leading to his 1982 international breakthrough.
family_context_summary: Born in Antwerp, Belgium in a poor part of the city. His father was a biologist and municipal gardener who took him on drawing trips to the Antwerp Zoo and to the Rubens House, nurturing his interest in art and nature.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a biologist/municipal gardener who introduced Fabre to both art (Rubens) and natural science (insects, animals), directly shaping his artistic themes. His mother introduced him to French chanson music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Antwerp art scene, father's biological influence, early performance art, avant-garde theatre movement
evidence_summary: Fabre grew up in a poor neighborhood of Antwerp but benefited from his father's dual influence of biology and art, which shaped his unique artistic language around insects and the body. He attended the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Antwerp and began performing while still a student. The Antwerp art scene and the broader European performance art movement of the late 1970s provided context for his rapid rise. His 1982 breakthrough at age 24 established him internationally.
starting_point: Born in a poor neighborhood of Antwerp, Belgium to a biologist/municipal gardener father who nurtured his interest in art and nature through trips to the zoo and Rubens House.
current_position: Multidisciplinary artist (visual art, theatre, writing); founded Troubleyn theatre company in 1986; first living artist to present a large-scale exhibition at the Louvre (2008); continues to work from Antwerp.

trajectory.event: Created first performance art pieces as a student in Antwerp, including window performances and street renaming actions.
Began career as stage director with 'Theater geschreven met een K is een kater' and conducted Money Performances.
Achieved international breakthrough with 'This is theatre as it was to be expected and foreseen'.
Commissioned for the Venice Biennale with 'The Power of Theatrical Madness'.
Established the Troubleyn/Jan Fabre theatre company in Antwerp.
Became the first living artist to present a large-scale exhibition at the Louvre in Paris.
Major exhibition at the State Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg.

name: Nikola Karabatic
milestone_by_age_26: Won the EHF Champions League with Montpellier in 2003 at age 19, scoring 11 goals in the first leg of the final, and was French champion four consecutive years (2002-2005).
early_history_summary: Karabatic was born in Yugoslavia to a Croatian father who was a professional handball player and coach. The family moved to France when Nikola was 3.5 years old for his father's coaching job. He began training with his father at age 8 in Frontignan, joined the Montpellier academy as a teenager, and made his professional debut at 17 in 2001. He won the French championship in his first season and the Champions League at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to Branko Karabatic, a Croatian professional handball player who became a coach in France, and Radmila, a Serbian mother. The family moved to France for the father's coaching position when Nikola was young. His younger brother Luka is also a professional handball player.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional handball player and coach who directly trained Nikola from age 8, providing deep domain immersion and technical knowledge from the start.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father handball coach, Montpellier academy, early professional debut, French handball ecosystem
evidence_summary: Karabatic was born into a handball family: his father Branko was a professional player who became a coach in France, directly training Nikola from age 8. This gave him deep domain proximity and elite coaching from the start. He joined Montpellier, one of France's top clubs, as a teenager and made his professional debut at 17. By 19, he had won the EHF Champions League and multiple French championships, benefiting from both his father's expertise and the elite French handball pipeline.
starting_point: Born in Niš, Yugoslavia to a Croatian father who was a professional handball player and coach and a Serbian mother; family moved to France when he was 3.5 for his father's coaching position.
current_position: Retired from professional handball in 2024; widely regarded as one of the greatest handball players of all time; 3-time IHF World Player of the Year (2007, 2014, 2016).

trajectory.event: Made debut for the French national team and won first French championship with Montpellier.
Won EHF Champions League with Montpellier, scoring 11 goals in the first leg of the final against Portland San Antonio.
Won European Championship gold with France.
Won EHF Champions League with THW Kiel and was named IHF World Player of the Year for the first time.
Won Olympic gold medal with France at the Beijing Olympics.
Won World Championship gold with France.
Named IHF World Player of the Year for the second time.
Won Olympic gold with France at Rio and was named IHF World Player of the Year for the third time.

name: Svetlana Alexievich
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Alexievich was working as a journalist at local newspapers in Belarus. Her first book, 'War's Unwomanly Face', was not published until 1985 when she was 37.
early_history_summary: Alexievich worked as a reporter at a local newspaper in Narovl after finishing school, then studied journalism at Minsk University from 1967 to 1972. After graduation she worked at local newspapers in Beresa and then Minsk. She began collecting material for her first book in the 1970s but did not publish it until 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in Ivano-Frankovsk, Ukraine to a Belarusian father and Ukrainian mother, both schoolteachers. The family moved to Belarus after her father's demobilization from the army.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were schoolteachers, and her grandfather was also a rural schoolteacher. The family tradition was in education, not specifically in journalism or literature.
evidence_summary: Alexievich spent her twenties as a local newspaper journalist in Belarus with no significant literary milestone. Her Nobel Prize-winning oral history work emerged over decades, with her first book published at age 37. At 26, she was a working journalist with no notable publication or recognition.

name: Nora Mørk
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold at the 2010 European Women's Handball Championship with Norway at age 19, and won the EHF Champions League with Larvik HK in 2011 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Mørk started playing handball at Bækkelaget from age 6 and made her senior debut at 16. She played for Bækkelaget, Aalborg DH, and Njård IL before joining Larvik HK in 2009 at age 18. She debuted for the Norwegian national team on September 21, 2010, and won gold at the European Championship that year. In 2011, she won the EHF Champions League with Larvik.
family_context_summary: Born in Oslo, Norway. Started playing handball at Bækkelaget from age 6. Family background beyond this is not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian handball ecosystem, Larvik HK, early senior debut, Bækkelaget youth system
evidence_summary: Mørk grew up in Oslo immersed in Norway's dominant women's handball culture, starting at Bækkelaget at age 6 and reaching senior level by 16. She joined Larvik HK, one of Norway's top clubs, at 18, and the Norwegian national team at 19. Norway's position as the world's leading women's handball nation provided an elite performance pipeline. She was recognized as an exceptional talent from a young age, described as 'completely outstanding' relative to her age group.
starting_point: Born in Oslo, Norway; started playing handball at Bækkelaget from age 6, making her senior debut at 16. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Plays for Team Esbjerg in Denmark and the Norwegian national team; six-time EHF Champions League winner; Olympic gold medalist (2024 Paris); one of Norway's most decorated handball players.

trajectory.event: Debuted for the Norwegian national team and won gold at the European Women's Handball Championship.
Won the EHF Champions League with Larvik HK.
Won European Championship gold with Norway after returning from multiple knee surgeries; selected as All-Star right back.
Won World Championship gold with Norway; again selected as All-Star right back.
Won Olympic bronze with Norway at Rio 2016 as tournament top goalscorer.
Won European Championship gold with Norway as tournament top scorer and All-Star right back.
Won Olympic gold medal with Norway at the Paris Olympics.

name: Barbara Wagner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Championship in pairs skating with partner Robert Paul in 1957 at age 19, the first of four consecutive world titles (1957-1960).
early_history_summary: Wagner was paired with Robert Paul in 1952 at age 14 by coach Sheldon Galbraith at the Toronto Skating Club. They won the Canadian championship for five consecutive years (1955-1960), North American champions for three (1957-1959), and World champions for four (1957-1960). They placed 6th at the 1956 Olympics before winning gold at the 1960 Olympics. Wagner was 19 when she won her first World Championship.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources beyond her birth location.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sheldon Galbraith coaching, Robert Paul partnership, Toronto Skating Club, Canadian figure skating system
evidence_summary: Wagner was paired with Robert Paul at age 14 by Sheldon Galbraith, one of Canada's most elite figure skating coaches, at the Toronto Skating Club. Galbraith had previously coached Olympic champion Barbara Ann Scott and world champions Dafoe and Bowden. The sustained, high-quality coaching and the exceptional complementary partnership with Paul over eight years were the primary drivers of their dominance. Canada's strong figure skating tradition provided a supportive ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada; paired with Robert Paul at age 14 under coach Sheldon Galbraith at the Toronto Skating Club. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive skating after 1960 Olympics; worked as coach and principal coach of the Ice Follies; inducted into World Figure Skating Hall of Fame in 1980; resides in Atlanta, Georgia.

trajectory.event: Won first World Championship in pairs with Robert Paul, beginning a four-year reign as world champions.
Won the Lou Marsh Trophy as Canada's top athlete with partner Robert Paul.
Won Olympic gold medal in pairs at Squaw Valley with all seven judges awarding first place.
Began professional career skating with the Ice Capades.
Inducted into the World Figure Skating Hall of Fame.

name: Bono
milestone_by_age_26: U2's album 'War' reached #1 on the UK Albums Chart in March 1983 when Bono was 23, knocking Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' from the top spot; the band had already released two prior albums by that point.
early_history_summary: Bono responded to a bulletin board advertisement at Mount Temple Comprehensive School in Dublin in September 1976, joining the band that became U2 at age 16. The band won a talent contest in Limerick and was signed to CBS Records Ireland. U2 released their debut album 'Boy' in 1980 when Bono was 20, followed by 'October' in 1981 and 'War' in 1983, which became their first #1 UK album.
family_context_summary: Born in Dublin, Ireland to a Catholic postal worker father and a Protestant mother who died when Bono was 14. Grew up in the working-class Ballymun/Finglas area in a mixed-faith household during the Troubles.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a postal worker who was also a talented painter and singer but was confined by circumstances. No direct music industry domain transfer from parents.
primary_early_advantage_tags: U2 schoolmate formation, The Edge partnership, post-punk wave, Dublin music scene, mother's death
evidence_summary: Bono grew up in a working-class Dublin household with a postal worker father and lost his mother at 14, creating adversity that fueled his artistic drive. The formation of U2 with schoolmates at Mount Temple Comprehensive School, particularly the complementary partnership with guitarist The Edge, was the key early advantage. The post-punk/new wave movement of the late 1970s and early 1980s provided a structural wave, and manager Paul McGuinness offered early mentorship. The band's relentless touring and Dublin's emerging music scene built their audience from the ground up.
starting_point: Born to a Catholic postal worker father and Protestant mother in Dublin, Ireland; grew up in the working-class Ballymun/Finglas area; mother died when he was 14.
current_position: Lead singer of U2; estimated net worth ~$700M; activist and philanthropist; co-founder of ONE Campaign and (RED); lives in Dublin and the south of France.

trajectory.event: Co-founded U2 with schoolmates at Mount Temple Comprehensive School in Dublin.
U2 released debut album 'Boy' on Island Records.
U2's album 'War' reached #1 on the UK Albums Chart, knocking Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' from the top spot.
U2 released 'The Unforgettable Fire', produced by Brian Eno, marking a new artistic direction.
U2 released 'The Joshua Tree', becoming global superstars; album debuted at #1 in both UK and US.
Named TIME Person of the Year; U2 inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Published memoir 'Surrender: 40 Songs, One Story'.

name: Eva Herzigová
milestone_by_age_26: Became the face of the Wonderbra 'Hello Boys' campaign in 1994 at age 21, one of the most iconic advertising campaigns of the decade, establishing her as a leading supermodel.
early_history_summary: Herzigová grew up in Litvínov, Czechoslovakia, the daughter of an electrician and an accountant. She won a modeling contest organized by Metropolitan Models in Prague at age 16 in 1989 and moved to Paris. She became the face of Guess jeans by age 20, which led to the breakthrough Wonderbra campaign in 1994. By her mid-twenties she was one of the prominent supermodels of the 1990s.
family_context_summary: Born in Litvínov, Czechoslovakia to an electrician father and accountant/secretary mother. Grew up in a small mountain village with limited exposure to Western fashion. Parents supported her modeling career but advised her to have a backup plan.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to fashion or modeling. Father worked as an electrician at a mining company; mother was a secretary/accountant.
primary_early_advantage_tags: exceptional physical attributes, supermodel era, Metropolitan Models, Paris fashion capital, communist Czechoslovakia background
evidence_summary: Herzigová grew up in communist Czechoslovakia with working-class parents and no fashion industry connections. Her exceptional physical attributes (height of 5'11", striking features) were the primary catalyst for her career when she won a modeling contest at 16. Moving to Paris provided access to the elite fashion ecosystem, and the 1990s supermodel wave created a structural opportunity. The Wonderbra campaign in 1994 catapulted her to international fame, making her part of the supermodel phenomenon alongside Naomi Campbell and Cindy Crawford.
starting_point: Born to an electrician father and accountant mother in Litvínov, Czechoslovakia; grew up in a small mountain village with limited exposure to Western fashion or culture.
current_position: Model, actress, and fashion journalist; lives in Italy with businessman Gregorio Marsiaj and their three sons; estimated net worth ~$12M; continues to model and serve as brand ambassador.

trajectory.event: Won a modeling contest in Prague organized by French agency Metropolitan Models and moved to Paris.
Became the face of Guess jeans, following in the footsteps of Claudia Schiffer.
Became the face of the Wonderbra 'Hello Boys' campaign, achieving international fame as a supermodel.
Married Bon Jovi drummer Tico Torres; featured in the Pirelli Calendar.
Walked in Yves Saint Laurent's farewell show in Paris.
Birth of first son George with partner Gregorio Marsiaj.

name: Charles Dutoit
milestone_by_age_26: Made his professional conducting debut on January 9, 1959 at age 22 with the Lausanne Chamber Orchestra with Martha Argerich as soloist, and served as guest conductor of the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande from 1959.
early_history_summary: Dutoit was born in Lausanne, Switzerland and began studying violin at age 11. He first conducted at age 14 in a small chamber orchestra. He studied at the Lausanne Conservatory, then won first prize in conducting at the Geneva Conservatory in 1958, and studied at the Accademia Chigiana in Siena and at Tanglewood with Charles Munch. He made his professional conducting debut in January 1959 and became a guest conductor of the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande.
family_context_summary: Born in Lausanne, Switzerland. His father was a cavalry instructor who lost everything during the Great Depression. His grandmother on his mother's side was from the region, and his father hailed from Savoy. The family was not wealthy.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to music. Father was a cavalry instructor; Dutoit was initially more interested in math and science than music, starting music only at age 11.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Geneva Conservatory, Tanglewood, Ernest Ansermet mentorship, Lausanne Conservatory, Swiss classical music tradition
evidence_summary: Dutoit came from a non-musical family that had lost its wealth in the Great Depression, but he gained access to elite musical training through the Swiss conservatory system. He studied at the Lausanne Conservatory, Geneva Conservatory (first prize in conducting), the Accademia Chigiana in Siena, and Tanglewood with Charles Munch. He had personal acquaintance with Ernest Ansermet and worked with Karajan at Lucerne. This dense network of elite institutional training and mentorship enabled his professional debut at 22. His childhood friendship with child prodigy conductor Roberto Benzi also provided early peer inspiration.
starting_point: Born in Lausanne, Switzerland to a cavalry instructor father who lost everything in the Great Depression; started music at age 11, initially more interested in math and science.
current_position: Retired conductor; former music director of the Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal (1977-2002) and artistic director of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra; career effectively ended in 2017-2018 amid sexual assault allegations from multiple women.

trajectory.event: Won first prize in conducting at the Geneva Conservatory and studied at the Accademia Chigiana in Siena.
Made professional conducting debut on January 9 with the Lausanne Chamber Orchestra with Martha Argerich as soloist.
Became music director of the Bern Symphony Orchestra, serving for 11 years.
Became music director of the Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal, leading it to international recognition over 25 years.
First conducted the Philadelphia Orchestra, beginning a long association.
Became artistic director and principal conductor of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra in London.
Stepped down from the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra amid sexual assault allegations from multiple women; major orchestras worldwide severed ties.

name: Wang Hao
milestone_by_age_26: Won the men's singles silver medal at the 2004 Athens Olympics at age 20, and won men's singles titles at the Asian Championships, national championship, and ITTF World Tour Grand Finals in 2003 at age 19-20.
early_history_summary: Wang Hao was born in Changchun, Jilin Province, China and began table tennis training at age 7 after his father saw a TV advertisement for a children's program. He trained under coach Liu Hongqi and was exceptionally admitted to the Changchun City Sports School at age 10. He joined the Bayi (military) team at 13, was selected for the national second team in 1998, and promoted to the first team in 2000. By 2003, he was winning major international titles, and in 2004 he won Olympic silver in singles at Athens.
family_context_summary: Born in Changchun, Jilin Province, China to an ordinary family. His father Wang Zhongquan introduced him to table tennis at age 7 after seeing a TV advertisement and made strategic decisions about his training path, including declining lucrative club offers to place him in the Bayi military team.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was not a table tennis professional but recognized his son's talent early and actively managed his training trajectory, including selecting coaches and declining commercial offers in favor of the military team pathway.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese national team system, Bayi military team, early specialization, coach Liu Hongqi, Changchun sports school
evidence_summary: Wang Hao grew up in an ordinary Chinese family but was channeled into the elite Chinese table tennis pipeline from age 7. His father made strategic decisions about his training, placing him with coach Liu Hongqi and later in the Bayi military team rather than commercial clubs. China's position as the undisputed epicenter of world table tennis provided the highest-level training environment and competitive ecosystem. He was recognized as an exceptional talent, being exceptionally admitted to the city sports school at age 10 and reaching the national team by 15. The intensive, concentrated training of the Chinese national team system was the dominant advantage.
starting_point: Born in Changchun, Jilin Province, China to an ordinary family; father introduced him to table tennis at age 7 after seeing a TV advertisement for a children's training program.
current_position: Retired Chinese table tennis player; current head coach of the Chinese Men's Table Tennis Team; multiple-time world champion and three-time Olympic singles silver medalist.

trajectory.event: Selected for the Chinese national table tennis second team.
Won men's singles titles at the Asian Championships, national championship, and ITTF World Tour Grand Finals.
Won Olympic silver medal in men's singles at the Athens Olympics.
Won Olympic team gold at Beijing; won silver in men's singles.
Won world championship in men's singles at the Yokohama World Table Tennis Championships.
Inducted into the ITTF Hall of Fame.
Won Olympic team gold at London; retired from competitive play.
